cells.quote: Knowledge levels regarding O2 toxicity differed significantly among professional groups (p = 0.001). The proportion of those who stated that they had knowledge on this issue was 84.3% among resident physicians and 88.1% among attending physicians, whereas it was 60.2% among nurses.
cells.note: The study reports a significant overall group difference and higher awareness among resident physicians than nurses, but does not print a pairwise effect size.

D.comparison: pre-training period without systematic simulation training

O.outcome_detail: documented interruption of oxytocin infusion during shoulder dystocia management

cells.quote: The interruption of oxytocin infusion (0% vs 15.8%, p < 0.001) and successful posterior arm delivery (11.3% vs 23.4%, p = 0.04) were documented significantly more often in the post‐training period.
cells.note: The authors state that documentation improved and attribute this partly to implementation of a fill-in shoulder dystocia checklist and emphasis on documentation during simulation training.
